input: Create a golangci-lint v2 config with exactly govet, staticcheck, errcheck and nolintlint. Add gofumpt with extra rules, a 5 minute timeout, and errcheck type assertion checks.
rubric: Uses version "2", linters.default none, and exactly the requested linters under linters.enable.
Places gofumpt and extra-rules under formatters, timeout under run, and errcheck options under linters.settings.
Enables nolintlint require-specific and require-explanation explicitly and proposes verification with the installed binary.

input: Our v1 .golangci.yml fails after moving to v2. It has linters-settings and gofumpt in linters.enable. We need to preserve the existing checks. What should change?
rubric: Checks versions and migration help, preserves original config, and uses migrate with review of the diff.
Explains v2 settings placement and formatter separation without silently dropping incompatible checks.
Requires config verification and an actual analysis run; does not equate schema validity with a clean repository.

input: Interpret these findings: handler.go:42 unchecked DB.Close error (errcheck); handler.go:55 response body must be closed (bodyclose); auth.go:12 validateToken unused (unused); auth.go:30 complexity 17 > 13 (gocyclo). No code context is available.
rubric: Explains each analyzer and seeks code context rather than declaring all findings false positives or blindly suppressing.
Does not delete validateToken without considering missing authentication wiring.
Treats complexity as a policy signal and ownership/error paths as code-dependent correctness questions.

input: We have bare //nolint directives and some with explanations that just say legacy code. Configure automatic checks and tell us which exceptions are justified.
rubric: Shows linters.settings.nolintlint with require-specific true, require-explanation true, and detection of unused directives.
Distinguishes checking explanation presence from verifying its truth; legacy status is not proof of safety.
Requires code evidence for correctness/security exceptions and prefers narrow scope.

input: Standalone staticcheck still reports SA1019 even though I added //nolint:staticcheck. We cannot migrate this API until an upstream dependency releases its replacement. How do I handle this?
rubric: Identifies the runner mismatch and uses Staticcheck lint:ignore SA1019 with an actual reason rather than claiming nolint works.
Records the compatibility blocker and removal condition and verifies the relevant diagnostic.

input: Our branch has six commits and 2000 old lint findings. Can we set new-from-rev HEAD~1 and call it clean? We also want quick autofixes.
rubric: Explains that HEAD~1 misses earlier branch changes and selects a deliberate available base or merge base.
Distinguishes filtered reporting from full cleanliness and preserves backlog visibility.
Uses scoped autofix with diff review and reruns rather than concurrent writers or blanket suppressions.

input: golangci-lint outputs no issues but exits nonzero with context deadline exceeded. Should we exclude half the directories to make it pass?
rubric: Does not call the repository clean; records failed analysis and examines configured timeout/version and verbose diagnostics.
Does not claim report exclusions reliably skip analysis or solve performance.
Distinguishes memory pressure concurrency tuning from a generic speedup.

input: A Go repo has two modules in a go.work. I changed one file in each. Can I run golangci-lint on just those two filenames and use --fix in a background agent while editing them?
rubric: Uses the intended module/package scope and build context rather than isolated filenames.
Avoids simultaneous writers to the same files and reviews autofix changes.
Reports analyzed scope rather than claiming all workspace packages are covered.
